Chapter 10: The Ongoing Struggle—Instinct, Order, and the Human Condition.
You know, there’s never really a final answer to that push and pull between what you want and what society expects from you. It’s an ongoing struggle—woven right into the fabric of everyday life. In your own way, you’re always searching for that sweet spot between following your instincts and sticking to order, chasing freedom and taking on responsibility, balancing your own needs with those of your community.
Imagine standing at a crossroads. One path calls you to follow your own desires. The other? It’s all about living up to what others expect. But the truth is, the choice is hardly ever black and white. There are risks and rewards no matter which way you turn, and honestly, the “right” direction can shift from one day—or even one moment—to the next.
Some days, your instincts just take over. Maybe you crave a little pleasure, a bit of adventure, or even just a chance to escape. On other days, you might feel that need for order, or a stronger pull toward connection with others. Most of the time, though, you’re just moving between the two—constantly negotiating that balance as best as you can.
Civilization gives us all sorts of tools to help manage this struggle—things like laws, customs, art, religion, even the communities we build together. These tools help channel our instincts in ways that support everyone, not just ourselves. But they do come at a cost. There’s always that little bit of discomfort, that sense that something you want is just out of reach.
But don’t mistake that discomfort for failure. It’s actually a sign of the richness and complexity of being human. We’re not meant to be perfectly satisfied or completely free. The tension between what we desire and the order we need is what makes us grow, pushes us to be creative, and brings us closer to each other.
The real challenge? It’s learning to accept this struggle without letting it overwhelm you. To see that the search for happiness isn’t about making all discomfort disappear—but about finding meaning, even when things feel unsettled. And while this isn’t always easy, it’s a journey that every single person faces, each in their own unique way.
